verdict.rationale: Sprinto documents user-built ingestion workflows, including creating them with an AI Editor from natural-language prompts. Those workflows can be triggered by incoming webhooks, and the platform also runs continuous monitoring, alerting, evidence collection and configurable AI risk auto-scoring in the background. However, the docs show only event-triggered ingestion and vendor-defined monitoring, not a general user-configurable autonomous automation engine. missing for 10: user-defined recurring schedules or triggers beyond ingestion webhooks, documentation of what configured automations can do autonomously (actions, conditions, run history), independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Sprinto’s AI Editor helps you create and modify ingestion workflows using natural language prompts.
You can use webhooks to: Receive incoming payloads, Trigger ingestion workflows, Process external events
Audit readiness by design: Maintain readiness with continuous monitoring, alerts, and evidence collection.
You can configure: AI risk auto-scoring, Risk thresholds and scoring levels
